1. Case 1: Neonatal lupus erythematosus
The 5-day-old neonate has widespread jaundice, third-degree AV block, annular periorbital rash, splenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and cholestatic hepatitis. Negative TORCH, viral, culture, and metabolic tests make congenital infection unlikely. Autoimmune serology showing ANA 1:640 and anti-Ro/SSA/anti-La/SSB >4 is highly specific for neonatal lupus erythematosus, supported by the maternal photosensitivity history. The graph links these findings (nodes 3, 4, 5, 10) to the neonatal lupus hypothesis (node 6), while refuting congenital infection. Cholestatic liver disease and hemolytic disorder are partial but less favored. Thus the diagnosis is neonatal lupus erythematosus.
